title: Getting started with colvR
text: consider dataset counts collected nn sites across pp years. Let YijY_{ij} denote number individuals recorded site ∈{1,…,n}\\{1,\dots,n\} year j∈{1,…,p}j \\{1,\dots,p\}. observation associated covariate vector xij∈ℝdx_{ij} \\mathbb{R}^d. full covariate matrix X∈ℝnp×dX \\mathbb{R}^{np \times d} typically combines three types information: Site-level covariates (R∈ℝn×d1R \\mathbb{R}^{n \times d_1}): descriptors constant across years (e.g. habitat type, geographic attributes). Year-level covariates (C∈ℝp×d2C \\mathbb{R}^{p \times d_2}): descriptors varying across years shared across sites (e.g. climate indices, survey effort). Site–year covariates (E∈ℝnp×d3E \\mathbb{R}^{np \times d_3}): descriptors specific site–year combination (e.g. water level, vegetation cover, observer identity). blocks concatenated : X=[R⊗𝟏p𝟏n⊗CE],d=d1+d2+d3, X = [R \otimes \mathbf{1}_p \;\;\; \mathbf{1}_n \otimes C \;\;\; E],  \qquad d = d_1 + d_2 + d_3,  observation (,j)(,j) described covariate vector xijx_{ij}. Zero-Inflated Poisson Log-Normal Probabilistic PCA (ZI-PLN-PCA) model generates abundances two steps: Presence/absence process Uij∼Bernoulli(πij),πij=11+exp⁡(−xij⊤γ), U_{ij} \sim \text{Bernoulli}\!\left(\pi_{ij}\right),  \qquad \pi_{ij} = \frac{1}{1+\exp(-x_{ij}^\top \gamma)},  Uij=0U_{ij}=0 deterministically yields Yij=0Y_{ij}=0. parameter vector γ\gamma encodes covariates affect probability presence. Abundance process conditional presence Yij∼Poisson(exp(xij⊤β+Zij)), Y_{ij} \;\sim\; \text{Poisson}\!\left(\exp(x_{ij}^\top \beta + Z_{ij})\right),  β\beta controls covariate effects abundance, ZijZ_{ij} latent Gaussian effect. site ii associated qq-dimensional latent vector Wi∼𝒩(0,Iq),Zi=CWi,C∈ℝp×q, W_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0,I_q),  \qquad Z_i = C W_i, \quad C \\mathbb{R}^{p \times q},  covariance structure latent effects Σ=CC⊤. \Sigma = C C^\top . low-rank formulation parallels probabilistic PCA parsimoniously captures correlations years within site.

title: Getting started with colvR
text: illustrate use colvR, rely dataset waterbird provided package. contains counts waterbird species monitoring program covering several sites several years. data incomplete: many site-year combinations surveyed. Together high proportion zeros, substantial amount missing values makes dataset suitable case study zero-inflated Poisson log-normal framework implemented colvR. Sites years anonymized.
code: data("waterbird") Y <- waterbird$Y ; X <- waterbird$X n <- nrow(Y) ; p <- ncol(Y) ; d <- ncol(X)  cat(mean(is.na(Y)), "is the proportion of missing entries in Y.\n") #> 0.4443353 is the proportion of missing entries in Y. cat(mean(Y == 0, na.rm = TRUE), "is the proportion of 0's in Y.\n") #> 0.6705407 is the proportion of 0's in Y.

what: Choosing the size of the latent space
title: Getting started with colvR
text: important step model specification choice dimension qq latent space. function select_model_bic() can used compare models fitted different values qq, based Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC). selected value corresponds latent space dimension maximizes BIC score. rely precomputed model selection (saved package) keep vignette fast. want recompute locally, set Sys.setenv(COLVR_RECOMPUTE = "true") knitting. Model selection via BIC
code: q_grid <- 1:p  use_precomputed <- !identical(Sys.getenv("COLVR_RECOMPUTE"), "true")  if (use_precomputed) {   sel <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "sel_waterbird.rds", package = "colvR")) } else {   sel <- select_model_bic(Y, X, Miss.ZIPLNPCA, q_grid) }  q <- sel$q_star q #> [1] 11 plot(q_grid, sel$values, type = "b",      xlab = "Latent dimension q", ylab = "BIC") points(q, max(sel$values), pch = 19, cex = 1.2) abline(v = q, lty = 2)

title: Getting started with colvR
text: latent dimension qq chosen, model fitted function Miss.ZIPLNPCA(). function estimates model parameters simultaneously imputing missing entries count matrix Y.select_model_bic() already returns model fitted selected qq, need fit : sel$fit_star equivalent toMiss.ZIPLNPCA(Y, X, q). returned object list containing: estimated parameters model (beta, gamma, C, …), variational parameters used inference, imputed count matrix, missing values Y replaced predictions. fitted object can explored inspect estimated parameters, check convergence, evaluate quality imputations.
code: fit <- sel$fit_star

title: Getting started with colvR
text: Beyond point estimates, colvR also provides tools quantify uncertainty parameters. function V_theta() computes estimate covariance matrix parameters, based sandwich estimator. Using , can derive approximate confidence intervals regression coefficients presence (γ) abundance (β) models. now display point estimates 95% confidence intervals regression coefficients presence model (γ\gamma) abundance model (β\beta). Regression coefficients 95% confidence intervals
code: cov <- V_theta(Y, X, fit) theta <- c(fit$mStep$gamma, fit$mStep$beta) var <- diag(cov)[1:(2*d)] Intervals <- IC(theta, var) # Build a compact table of estimates and 95% CIs (no dependency on IC()) se <- sqrt(var) par_names <- c(paste0("gamma_", seq_len(d)), paste0("beta_", seq_len(d))) ci_tab <- data.frame(   param = par_names,   estimate = theta,   lo = theta - 1.96 * se,   hi = theta + 1.96 * se,   group = rep(c("gamma (presence)", "beta (abundance)"), each = d),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )  # Order for plotting: gamma first, then beta, top-to-bottom ci_tab$param_pretty <- factor(ci_tab$param, levels = rev(ci_tab$param))  op <- par(mar = c(5, 10, 2, 2)) plot(   x = ci_tab$estimate, y = as.numeric(ci_tab$param_pretty),   xlab = "Coefficient (estimate with 95% CI)", ylab = "",   yaxt = "n", pch = 19, xaxs = "i", col = ifelse(ci_tab$group == "gamma (presence)", "black", "gray30") ) segments(ci_tab$lo, as.numeric(ci_tab$param_pretty),          ci_tab$hi, as.numeric(ci_tab$param_pretty),          lwd = 2, col = ifelse(ci_tab$group == "gamma (presence)", "black", "gray30")) abline(v = 0, lty = 2) axis(2, at = seq_along(levels(ci_tab$param_pretty)), labels = levels(ci_tab$param_pretty), las = 1) legend("bottomright", inset = 0.01, bty = "n",        legend = c("gamma (presence)", "beta (abundance)"),        pch = 19, col = c("black", "gray30")) par(op)

title: colvR
text: basic example shows solve common problem:
code: library(colvR) #>  #> Attachement du package : 'colvR' #> L'objet suivant est masqué depuis 'package:stats': #>  #>     BIC  n <- 1500 ; p <- 30 ; q <- 4 ; d <- 4 dim <- list(n = n, p = p, d = d, q = q) X <- cbind(rep(1, n*p), rnorm(n*p), rep(rnorm(n), p)) trend <- rep(1:p, each = n) X <- cbind(X, scale(trend)) B <- c(2, 0.7, 0.5, -0.6) ; D <- c(-0.5, 0.5, 0.4, -0.4) ; C <- matrix(rnorm(p*q)/2, nrow = p, ncol = q) theta <- list(B = B, D = D, C = C)  sim <- Simul(X, theta, dim) ; Y <- sim$Y  fit <- Miss.ZIPLNPCA(Y, X, q)

what: BIC from the ELBO for PLN-PCA and ZIP-PLN-PCA models — BIC
title: BIC from the ELBO for PLN-PCA and ZIP-PLN-PCA models — BIC
text: Computes BIC-like score log-likelihood replaced ELBO fitted model (higher better): $$\mathrm{BIC} = \mathrm{ELBO} - \frac{\log(n)}{2}\Big[q\{p - (q-1)/2\} + k\Big],$$ \(q\{p - (q-1)/2\}\) number free parameters \(C\) (identifiable rotation) \(k\) number regression parameters: \(2d\) ZIP-PLN-PCA model (\(\beta\) \(\gamma\)), \(d\) PLN-PCA model vectorized design (\((np) \times d\)) \(pd\) rowwise design (\(n \times d\)). \(n\) number rows Y (sites), independent units model.

what: ICL from the ELBO for PLN-PCA and ZIP-PLN-PCA models — ICL
title: ICL from the ELBO for PLN-PCA and ZIP-PLN-PCA models — ICL
text: Integrated Completed Likelihood: BIC minus entropy variational distribution latent variables (higher better): $$\mathrm{ICL} = \mathrm{BIC} - \mathcal{H}(W) - \mathcal{H}(U).$$ \(\mathcal{H}(W)\): entropy Gaussian variational     distribution \(W\),     \(\frac{1}{2}\sum_{,k} \log \sigma^2_{ik} + \frac{nq}{2}\{1 + \log(2\pi)\}\),     \(\sigma^2 = S\) ZIP-PLN-PCA model (S     variance) \(\sigma^2 = S^2\) PLN-PCA model (S     standard deviation). Zero q = 0. \(\mathcal{H}(U)\): entropy Bernoulli variational     distribution \(U\),     \(-\sum_{ij} \{\xi_{ij}\log\xi_{ij} + (1-\xi_{ij})\log(1-\xi_{ij})\}\)     (ZIP-PLN-PCA model ).

code: set.seed(1) n <- 30; p <- 5; d <- 2; q <- 2 X <- cbind(1, rnorm(n * p))                       # (n*p) x d design theta <- list(B = matrix(c(1, 0.5)), D = matrix(c(1, -0.5)),               C = matrix(rnorm(p * q, sd = 0.5), p, q)) Y <- Simul(X, theta, list(n = n, p = p, d = d, q = q))$Y Y[sample(n * p, 20)] <- NA                        # missing entries  # \donttest{ sel <- select_model_bic(Y, X, Miss.ZIPLNPCA, latents = 1:3) sel$values #>         1         2         3  #> -265.5805 -267.4293 -272.9659  sel$q_star #> [1] 1 fit <- sel$fit_star  sel_icl <- select_model_bic(Y, X, Miss.ZIPLNPCA, latents = 1:3,                             criterion = "ICL") sel_icl$q_star #> [1] 1 # }
